meta.what: Round 8: can the no-war band of 'paid to Russia' (to_rus) be narrowed by measuring it on physical fuel volumes? Rolling back-tests on imports from Russia in TJ / kt (gas, crude, products, coal), 2005-2021, grouped by delivery infrastructure, combined with a non-fuel band through each country's fuel share and the measured joint errors. Contracts and infrastructure are listed as evidence.
meta.units: Multipliers in real (volume) terms, as cf_bands.json / to_rus_cf.json: cumulative_band = multiplier on the SUM over the horizon of the central expected level (H5_2026_8of12 = 2022-2026 with 2026 at 8/12); multiplier_vs_2021 = per-year ratio to the yearly central.
meta.central: 1.0 for every country (2021 held flat). Poland has a documented different path (Yamal gas contract not renewed after 2022); it is given separately as central_alternative and not applied.
meta.how_to_apply: Only for countries with status 'new': to_rus cb[1..5] = cumulative_band H1..H4 and H5_2026_8of12; yearly bmul_lo = bmul x multiplier_vs_2021.low, bmul_hi = bmul x multiplier_vs_2021.high. Countries with status 'kept_today' carry today's band unchanged (copied from site/data.json for reference). Base, actuals and central path unchanged.
meta.decision_rule: New band only if (a) the 2022-2026 band is >= 5% narrower than today's; (b) it is era-calibrated (5th-95th percentile of two eras of origins x K covers >= 90% of the third; eras 2005-09, 2010-12, 2013-16; K >= 1, no shrinking); (c) it covers >= 90% of the country's own 5-year windows (at least 8 measured) and all three of its test windows (origins 2007, 2012, 2016); (d) the band built WITHOUT the country also covers >= 90% of its windows; (e) safeguard: >= 90% of the country's own windows of the map's own series (deflated value, all goods) are inside, else the band is extended to cover them.
meta.fuel_volume_index: x_y = sum over fuels of volume x fixed 2019-2021 unit value: crude EUR 370/t, products EUR 420/t, pipeline gas EUR 4.67/GJ (EUR 4,670/TJ GCV), coal EUR 60/t. A constant-price volume index: price noise removed.
meta.groups: Infrastructure group fixed ex ante: 'pipeline' if pipeline gas + Druzhba crude is >= 60% of the fuel value bought from Russia (back-test windows: at the origin year, from the volumes; application: in 2019-2021, from energy2.json). LNG-only buyers: ESP PRT GBR JPN KOR IND CHN IRL MLT CYP. Druzhba crude: DEU POL CZE SVK HUN BLR (UKR excluded).
meta.scripts: Produced by the project's research step and kept as a data input; the research scripts are not in the repository, and the sources are listed in the notes. Data: Eurostat and Comtrade.

notes: Hypothesis holds for pipeline buyers, not for seaborne buyers: see fuel_volume_cf-notes.md.

Austria: Eurostat shows no gas from Russia after 2008 (origin not specified) and Russia's mirror is used only where units splice (factor 0.5-2); Austria's own windows cannot be measured, so it keeps today's band.
Belgium 2011-2016 gas, Bulgaria 2020-2021 crude, Belarus 2021 gas: reported zeros or collapses treated as confidentiality artefacts (missing).
Comtrade HS 2711 includes LPG; for neighbours (KGZ, ARM, MNG, KAZ) the "gas" series mixes natural gas and LPG.
The band is a volume band. The map applies it to a central that already carries the no-war price path (energy_nowar.json); price uncertainty is separate (nrl/nrh).

fuel_band._measured_on: fuel volume composite, pipeline group, 88 five-year windows, K = 1.65

nonfuel_band._measured_on: non-fuel imports from Russia deflated by the non-fuel index, all importers with >= EUR 0.1 bn, 450 windows, K = 1.75

DEU.method: 2021 level held (central 1.0). Band = joint distribution of the fuel-volume and non-fuel errors of the same country-windows in the 'pipeline' infrastructure group (rolling origins 2005-2016, 1-5 years), combined with this country's fuel share 0.789 (R = s*fuel + (1-s)*non-fuel), 5th-95th percentile x K = 1.25 (era-calibrated: two eras cover >= 90% of the third); low/high then extended to (0.738, 1.314) so that >= 90% of the country's own windows of the map's own series (deflated value) are covered.
evidence: Uniper contracts to 2035/36 (about 24 bcm/yr; take-or-pay about 0.36 of the 2021 volume, not binding); OMV, Wingas and others also held long-term contracts.
Nord Stream 2 (55 bcm/yr) never flowed; it was a new route for contracted gas, so the 2021-held volume is unchanged.
Druzhba crude to Schwedt and Leuna.

central_alternative.what: Documented pre-war path: Russian gas leaves Poland's imports after 2022 (non-renewal notified Nov 2019). Gas is 0.223 of Poland's fuel from Russia and fuel is 0.634 of the total, so the total falls to 1 - 0.634 x 0.223 = 0.859 of 2021 from 2023.

gas.pre_war_plan: PGNiG notified Gazprom on 15 Nov 2019 that it would not renew; Baltic Pipe (10 bcm/yr, Norway) planned from 1 Oct 2022

gas.route: TurkStream / Balkan Stream via Serbia, and via Austria
gas.pre_war_plan: signed 27 Sep 2021; Hungary's 2021 imports from Russia in Eurostat were about 7.2 bcm (276 PJ), so the contract alone is about 0.62 of the 2021 gas volume; Hungary bought more than the contract in 2023 (over 5.5 bcm)

gas.volume: about 20 bcm/yr under the extended contracts plus 4 bcm/yr via Nord Stream; about 24 bcm/yr in all
gas.pre_war_plan: extended Aug 2006; take-or-pay of about 85% x 24 bcm is about 0.36 of Germany's 2021 imports from Russia (about 57 bcm in Eurostat), so it does not bind the band

gas.volume: not published in primary sources; Gazprom reported 14.1 bcm 'supplied to Austria' in 2019 (includes hub deliveries for others)
gas.take_or_pay: 96% according to later press reports of the contract text

gas.route: via Germany; Nord Stream additional volumes

gas.take_or_pay: 90% (about 8.1 bcm); an arbitration award later let RWE Transgas reduce its uptake
gas.pre_war_plan: 8.1 bcm is about 0.93 of Czechia's 2021 imports from Russia (about 8.7 bcm in Eurostat), but the reduction right and resale make it a soft floor
no documented decision before the war to stop or renew; 1 bcm/yr Azeri gas contracted from 2021 (IGB opened Oct 2022)

gas.volume: Blue Stream 16 bcm/yr; TurkStream contracts 14 bcm/yr (BOTAS and seven private firms), 8 bcm/yr of which expired in 2021; BOTAS 5.75 bcm/yr via TurkStream to end-2025
gas.pre_war_plan: Turkiye's 2021 imports from Russia in Eurostat were about 26 bcm; contracts covering 2026 were not in place before the war

gas.volume: annual protocols; 18.8 bcm (2020), 19.8 bcm (2021) per Russia's customs
gas.end: price protocol for 2022 signed 1 Dec 2021 at USD 128.5 per 1000 m3 (unchanged from 2021)
never flowed: Bundesnetzagentur suspended certification on 16 Nov 2021; Germany halted certification on 22 Feb 2022 (background knowledge)
gas.pre_war_plan: a new route for gas already contracted, not new demand; it does not change the 2021-held volume

crude.link: Druzhba north to Germany (PCK Schwedt, TotalEnergies Leuna)
crude.facts: Leuna takes about 10 Mt/yr through Druzhba (2007 factbox); Rosneft contracts of 2013 for German buyers (Total, Shell, Eni shareholders of PCK) were to lift Rosneft's northern Druzhba exports to almost 13 Mt/yr; Schwedt was majority Rosneft-owned. Germany's crude from Russia was 27-38 Mt/yr in 2005-2021 (Eurostat).

crude.link: Druzhba north to Poland (Orlen Plock, Gdansk)
crude.facts: Orlen-Rosneft: about 18 Mt for Feb 2013-Jan 2016; 18-25.2 Mt for Feb 2016-Jan 2019; a later contract ran to Jan 2023. Orlen-Tatneft: 3.6-7.2 Mt for 2016-2018, later reported valid to end-2024. Both run past Feb 2022, so no pre-war break in Poland's crude path.

crude.link: Druzhba south to Slovakia and Hungary (MOL: Slovnaft Bratislava, Danube Szazhalombatta)
crude.facts: MOL's two main refineries have 14.2 Mt/yr capacity and most of their crude comes via Druzhba; Adria/JANAF alternative 11.8-14 Mt/yr. Slovakia's crude from Russia was 5.1-6.1 Mt every year 2005-2021 (Eurostat): the steadiest fuel series in the data.

crude.link: Druzhba south to Czechia (Unipetrol/Orlen Litvinov, Kralupy)
crude.facts: 54% of Czech refinery crude came through Druzhba (2012), the rest via TAL/IKL from Trieste; Orlen Unipetrol's first long-term contract with Rosneft in 2013.

24 Mt planned for 2020 but disrupted by a price dispute; the Belarusian government's range is 18-24 Mt/yr; 4.5 Mt planned for Q1 2021 (about 18 Mt/yr pace); no Russian crude to Naftan in Q3-Q4 2021 after US sanctions on Naftan. 2021 is therefore at the low end of the 18-24 Mt range, which argues against a band low much below 2021 for crude and allows upside.

summary.hypothesis: holds for pipeline buyers, fails for seaborne buyers
